govulncheck v1.1.4 (`make vuln`, seoy, 2026-10-21) reports one standard-library vulnerability:

- **GO-2026-6809** — Distrust compromised intermediate certificates in crypto/x509. Found in crypto/x509@go1.26.9, fixed in go1.26.10.
- Example trace: `chunked/fetch.go:207:24: chunked.VerifyDestTree calls io.Copy, which eventually calls x509.Certificate.Verify`.

This is not introduced by PR #44 (the trace is in existing `chunked` code); it appears on the current toolchain pin `go 1.26.9`. Fix: bump `go.mod` go/toolchain and the CI Go version to 1.26.10 in a separate change, then rerun `make vuln`.

Found during the W02.1b trust implementation on PR #44 (head 8c648e6e); left out of that PR to keep its scope bounded.

body:
Connected finding from #37 (sori#36), test coverage only. No behaviour bug is known.

In `authority/sqlitestore`, the #35 tests do not cover the connect-time busy wait. If `open` set the DSN `_busy_timeout` to the fixed 10 s instead of the time left, every current `TestOpen*` would still pass. The busy timeout recomputed before init masks it, because none of those tests hold a lock while the connection's `journal_mode` pragma runs.

#37 added `TestOpenCapsBusyWaitWhileConnecting` to `acquisition/sqlitecheckpoint`. It holds an exclusive lock on a rollback-journal file, so the connect pragma waits, and it uses a 300 ms budget. On seoy with go1.26.9:
- the uncapped-DSN mutant failed 3 of 3 runs, taking 10.0 s;
- the fix passed in 0.31 s.

Suggested: add the same test to `authority/sqlitestore/open_test.go`. Keep it out of #37 so the repo stays at one modifying PR.

Found during SQ-SORI-SM-W01 W01.2.issue36.corr1.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: authority/sqlitestore: no test for the connect-time busy wait cap

body:
Found during D02.2 E015 slice A measurement (Operator session c3466559, 2026-10-10, seoy, sorictl built from fc65a07a, controlled registry distribution 2.8.3). Corrected 2026-10-10 after independent review (Guardrail b35b1991, P2-1) by Operator c7d65e65: the first version said RSS grows with dataset size because of GC lag. That is wrong; see below.

**Fetch profile at fc65a07a:** chunk 1 GiB (default, no CLI knob), `fetchConcurrency = 4` (`chunked/fetch.go:21`, worker pool `:130-139`). `uploadConcurrency = 2` (`chunked/publish.go:26`) is the push side only.

**Observed fetch max RSS (GNU time, cold, ×1):**

| fixture | logical bytes L | files | in-flight 1 GiB buffers | fetch max RSS | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1-proof | 1,073,745,920 | 1 | 1 | 2,031,980 KiB (~1.94 GiB) | writer c3466559 |
| F10-unique | 10,737,418,240 | 8 × 1.25 GiB | 4 | 16,426,204 KiB (~15.7 GiB) | writer c3466559 |
| F4×1G default | 4 GiB | 4 × 1 GiB | 4 | 15,875,500 KiB (~15.1 GiB) | reviewer b35b1991 |
| F4×1G `GOGC=25` | 4 GiB | 4 × 1 GiB | 4 | 16,102,204 KiB | reviewer b35b1991 |
| F4×1G `GOMAXPROCS=1` | 4 GiB | 4 × 1 GiB | 4 (serialized) | 7,455,468 KiB | reviewer b35b1991 |

Push stays flat (12–19 MiB max RSS across L = 1/4/10 GiB). Byte equality PASS on every run.

**Memory: bounded by in-flight chunks × chunk size, not by L.** `reconstructFile` reads each chunk whole with `io.ReadAll` (`chunked/fetch.go:258`) before the digest check and `WriteAt`; chunks of one file are sequential, and up to 4 files run in parallel. So the peak is about `a × min(4, files) × chunk size`, with an observed `a` of ~1.8–1.9 (one buffer at a time) to ~3.8–3.9 (four in parallel). L = 4 GiB and L = 10 GiB peak at about the same RSS, and `GOGC=25` does not lower it, so this is live buffers, not GC lag. Levers are chunk size and fetchConcurrency. Even 256 MiB chunks at concurrency 4 would predict ~1.8–3.9 GiB (not measured), above the 768 MiB client budget, so a streaming fix is still needed: verify the digest while streaming (`io.TeeReader` into a hasher, write-through at the offset) instead of buffering the whole chunk.

**Disk: scales with L.** `volume_publish_fetch.go:965-980` copies the whole remote artifact into a temporary local OCI store under `os.TempDir()` before `fetchChunkedWithStaging` → `chunked.Fetch` (`:887`) materializes it. So a new destination needs ~L on `$TMPDIR`'s filesystem (possibly tmpfs, i.e. RAM) plus ~L on the destination filesystem. In the measurement both were on one filesystem (~2L written, 41,943,128 sectors for F10-unique). Dropping the full temp OCI copy bounds this.

**Impact:** D02.1/§6 design budgets (client RSS ≤ 768 MiB independent of L; download disk = staging L + journal, per filesystem) cannot be met by the current fetch path.

Not fixed here (measurement-only slice). Central assigns the W-unit owner.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: fetch: client RSS bounded by in-flight chunks x chunk size (fetchConcurrency 4, io.ReadAll per chunk); disk scales with L (full temp OCI copy)

## CURRENT CENTRAL DISPOSITION — 2026-09-10

**Status: PARTIAL / ORIGINAL PRIMARY GAPS CLOSED / BOUNDED TEST-EVIDENCE RESIDUALS OPEN.**

The original headline is stale in two important ways.

1. **Push-path credential-forwarding regression coverage is already fixed** by #12, including same-origin auth behavior and the GO-2026-5882 cross-host redirect class.
2. **A realistic registry push/pull smoke now runs in ordinary CI.** Current `.github/workflows/test.yml` provisions a `registry:2` service and runs `make smoke-cli` as `Registry Push/Pull Smoke` on push/pull_request. Therefore the old statement that no realistic registry cycle runs automatically is no longer true.

This issue remains open only for the residuals below. Do not use the old body as authority for already-completed work.

## Residual 1 — interrupted/partial push semantics are not yet proven

The current registry smoke proves a successful end-to-end push → inspect/fetch cycle, but it does not by itself prove behavior when a push fails after partial remote side effects have occurred.

The remaining question is not merely “does push return an error?” It is whether an interrupted upload can leave remote state that a retry later mistakes for a complete/accepted publication, and whether retry/reconcile behavior is deterministic.

This residual must remain subordinate to current Sori architecture:

- OCI/package transport success is **not** Asset Revision acceptance;
- current SORI-I1M authority-store acceptance and SORI-I2R representation relation own the semantic publication boundary;
- transport tests must not promote packaging metadata or a registry tag into Sori authority.

A future focused test may inject a failure after some registry-side work and prove the expected transport-level result/retry behavior without inventing new Sori authority semantics.

## Residual 2 — conditional skip governance is still misleading

Current `chunked/fetch_test.go` still contains unconditional `t.Skip(...)` cases such as:

```go
TestFetch_IntegrityFailure
TestFetch_SchemaVersionMismatch
```

with comments saying they are “covered in integration tests.” That statement must be revalidated against tests that actually execute the same branch. The existence of the new registry smoke does not automatically prove these low-level corruption/schema-injection branches.

Required outcome:

- remove a skip if a deterministic local test can cover the branch;
- otherwise make the missing profile/evidence explicit instead of letting a permanent skip look like coverage;
- do not add owner/expiry bureaucracy mechanically if the better solution is simply to make the test runnable.

## Residual 3 — in-fetch digest-mismatch branch needs branch-specific proof or explicit disposition

Sori has tree-integrity tests, including direct `VerifyDestTree` corruption coverage, but the historical audit specifically questioned whether the **in-fetch per-chunk mismatch branch** can be reached before lower-level OCI digest verification fails first.

Do not count a generic `err != nil` test or post-fetch tree corruption as proof of that exact branch. Either add branch-specific evidence, or document that the lower storage layer is the authoritative integrity fence and remove/dead-code-classify an unreachable duplicate check if that is what current code proves.

## Already closed from the original issue

- [x] Push auth / credential forwarding regression coverage (#12)
- [x] Realistic OCI registry push/pull smoke in normal CI (`registry:2` service + `make smoke-cli`)

## Current acceptance criteria

- [ ] Interrupted/partial push behavior has a focused test or an explicit current transport-level disposition.
- [ ] Retry after partial remote side effects cannot be misrepresented as a new authoritative Sori Revision solely because registry transport succeeded later.
- [ ] Historical unconditional `t.Skip` cases are either replaced with runnable tests or have truthful, current evidence ownership.
- [ ] The exact in-fetch digest-mismatch branch is proven reachable/tested, or its duplication/unreachability is explicitly resolved.
- [ ] OCI transport test wording remains separate from SORI-I1M acceptance and SORI-I2R representation authority.

## References

- Current Sori implementation-fit authority: https://app.notion.com/p/3d086e6dd1d1810e9acffe638163f475?pvs=204
- Current Authority Router: https://app.notion.com/p/3bf86e6dd1d18110938bc358e17c779e?pvs=204

**Implementation gate:** this is test/transport hardening, not permission to redesign Sori publication semantics. Fresh repo slot + current Sori authority must be checked before any modifying PR.
title: [PARTIAL · CURRENT] Push auth + registry smoke closed; interrupted-push and skip-governance residuals remain

body:
## Summary

Sori contains Tool/Volume proto definitions that overlap with NodeVault's active proto definitions.

Compared files:

```text
sori/tool_metadata.proto
sori/volume_resource.proto

NodeVault/protos/tool/ichthys/v1/tool_service.proto
NodeVault/protos/volres/ichthys/v1/volres_service.proto
```

Field-level comparison shows:

- six message shapes are field-compatible;
- `VolumeManifest` and `VolumeResource` have already diverged incompatibly;
- field numbers are reused with different meanings and, in one case, different protobuf wire types.

## Confirmed incompatibilities

### VolumeManifest

```text
field 4
Sori:      string format
NodeVault: uint64 total_size

field 5
Sori:      uint64 total_size
NodeVault: uint64 record_count
```

Field 4 is a wire-type conflict. Field 5 can parse successfully while silently assigning a value to the wrong semantic field.

### VolumeResource

Sori defines:

```text
id=1, basename=2, fullPath=3, isDirectory=4, size=5,
checksum=6, modTime=7, attrs=8, children=9
```

NodeVault defines:

```text
basename=1, full_path=2, is_directory=3, size=4, children=5
```

The field-number and semantic mappings are incompatible.

## Current risk level

This is classified P2 rather than P1 because the Sori proto files currently have no generated `.pb.go` code and no confirmed Go consumer. The active NodeVault→Sori dependency uses Sori Go packages, not these proto messages.

The immediate risk is therefore not an active wire outage. The risk is that a future attempt to generate or activate the Sori proto will introduce silent value corruption or decode failures.

## Required decision

Choose one:

1. remove the dead Sori proto definitions; or
2. designate a canonical contract owner and migrate Sori to the canonical descriptor with explicit compatibility handling.

Do not generate code from the current Sori definitions without resolving the field-number conflicts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The dead proto files are removed, or a canonical owner is documented.
- [ ] No duplicate Tool/Volume wire contract remains without a versioned ownership policy.
- [ ] Descriptor compatibility CI checks field numbers, types, package names, and reserved fields.
- [ ] If migration is required, old conflicting field numbers are reserved rather than reused.
- [ ] Tests demonstrate that Tool/Volume metadata cannot silently decode into different semantic fields.
- [ ] Sori's actual active NodeVault integration is documented separately from the removed/deprecated proto surface.

## Architecture impact

Canonical Architecture §12.1b and §20.9 classify this as F5, Confirmed/P2: inactive duplicate contract debt with existing field-number incompatibility.
title: [P2] Remove or canonicalize dead Tool/Volume proto definitions duplicated with NodeVault
